summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was admitted for severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, shortness of breath, and recent seizures following alcohol detox. He had been drinking heavily to manage withdrawal symptoms, which triggered an acute flare of pancreatitis and an asthma exacerbation. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control using IV then oral Dilaudid, benzodiazepines for alcohol withdrawal prophylaxis, and a steroid burst for asthma. His symptoms improved over three days—he stabilized neurologically, tolerated a low-fat diet, and had resolution of respiratory distress. He received IV iron for iron deficiency anemia and was discharged home with instructions to continue his medications, complete the prednisone course, maintain a low-fat diet, and follow up with his PCP, hepatologist, and dentist.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
